questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 6: Origins of Bright Crater Rays
Three students discuss why some young impact craters have bright rays extending across the surface.

Student 1: The rays consist mainly of fresh material excavated from beneath a dark, weathered surface. With time, exposure to radiation and tiny impacts darkens the rays until they resemble the surrounding ground.

Student 2: The material is not intrinsically brighter. Impact fragments roughen the surface, and the rough texture reflects sunlight toward the observer at certain angles. As small grains settle, the directional reflection weakens.

Student 3: Both excavation and texture matter. Fresh subsurface material begins brighter than the surface, and rough fragment deposits enhance that contrast. Weathering and settling therefore work together to fade the rays.

Which new evidence would most strongly support one student over the others?

options.F: A returned sample showing ray material is chemically similar to nearby surface material but has a much rougher texture would most strongly support Student 2.
options.G: An observation equally consistent with all viewpoints.
options.H: A restatement of the question without any measurement.
options.J: A result about a phenomenon no student discusses.

questions.explanation: The evidence directly favors the mechanism emphasized by one viewpoint.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE MATERIAL SET 4
Students tested how water temperature affected the time required for a tablet to dissolve. They used identical tablets, 103 mL of water in each cup, and stirred each cup at the same rate.

TABLE 1
Temperature (°C) | Dissolving time (s)
10 | 32
20 | 24
30 | 19
40 | 15

Trial 2 repeated the procedure with twice the water volume. Researcher 1 claims that higher temperature increases particle motion and therefore decreases dissolving time. Researcher 2 agrees that temperature matters but claims that stirring rate is the dominant factor whenever stirring is not controlled.

If changing stirring rate at constant temperature greatly changes dissolving time, the result most directly supports:

options.C: neither researcher because no variable changed
options.D: the claim that time cannot be measured

questions.explanation: The keyed response follows the material and directly targets 判断新证据支持哪一观点.
